hook: This spacecraft touched an asteroid for six seconds.
narration: This spacecraft just touched an asteroid.
NASA's OSIRIS-REx, coming down on a site called Nightingale, on Bennu.
A puff of gas kicks up rock and dust.
On Earth, at 6:08 p.m. Eastern, confirmation came in.
outcome: It touched Bennu for about six seconds, then backed away.
title: Spacecraft touches an asteroid
description:
On Oct. 20, 2020, NASA's OSIRIS-REx spacecraft touched down on asteroid Bennu at sample site Nightingale. Its SamCam imager recorded the approach, the touch and the burst of rock and dust.

Footage: NASA GSFC video, via the NASA Image and Video Library: https://images.nasa.gov/details/GSFC_20201021_M13745_TAG

question_comment: Would you have bet on a spacecraft landing on a pile of loose rocks?

facts.claim: SamCam images of the approach and touchdown on Bennu during TAG on Oct. 20
facts.source_quote: Captured on Oct. 20, during the OSIRIS-REx mission’s Touch-And-Go (TAG) sample collection event, this series of 82 images shows the SamCam imager’s field of view as the NASA spacecraft approaches and touches down on asteroid Bennu’s surface.

facts.claim: Came down to sample site Nightingale
facts.source_quote: The sampling event brought the spacecraft all the way down to sample site Nightingale
the team on Earth received confirmation of successful touchdown at 6:08 pm EDT

facts.claim: About six seconds, then a back-away burn
facts.source_quote: Preliminary data show the sampling head touched Bennu’s surface for approximately 6 seconds, after which the spacecraft performed a back-away burn.

visible_facts.claim: Sampling head descends onto the rocky surface and a burst of rock and dust erupts; control room team cheers
visible_facts.seen_at: source 23 to 36 s and 37 to 49 s
